summary: The Høgsenga Crags are high rock crags forming the northern extremity of Breplogen Mountain in the Mühlig-Hofmann Mountains of Queen Maud Land, Antarctica. They were mapped from surveys and air photos by the Sixth Norwegian Antarctic Expedition (1956–60), which gave them the name Høgsenga, meaning 'the high bed'.
one_line: Høgsenga Crags are rock crags at the northern end of Breplogen Mountain in Queen Maud Land, Antarctica.
key_facts: The Høgsenga Crags are high rock crags.
The Høgsenga Crags form the northern extremity of Breplogen Mountain.
Breplogen Mountain is located in the Mühlig-Hofmann Mountains of Queen Maud Land, Antarctica.
The Høgsenga Crags were mapped from surveys and air photos by the Sixth Norwegian Antarctic Expedition (1956–60).
The Høgsenga Crags were named by the Sixth Norwegian Antarctic Expedition (1956–60).
The name Høgsenga means 'the high bed'.
